results.excerpt: # Best PUMA Running Shoes: Which Model Should You Choose? When choosing running shoes, it's pretty obvious that the main thing you have to consider is how you're going to use them. Not all shoes are made equal. Some are built for speed, like lightweight race-day shoes. Others are designed to handle everyday training. Then there are shoes made for recovery runs or long miles, where cushioning and comfort matter most. Each one feels different once you get out on the road. PUMA has you covered, whatever kind of runner you are. With decades of experience designing performance footwear, they develop running shoes for different distances and training styles. Many models share technologies like NITRO™, but each one is tuned for a different type of run. This guide compares PUMA's key running shoes to help you find the best pair for your running goals. ## What is PUMA NITRO™ technology? PUMA NITRO™ technology is PUMA's nitrogen-infused ultra-light foam cushioning system, designed to make running shoes more responsive and energy efficient. The foam compresses when your foot lands, absorbs impact, then returns much of that energy during push-off to create a softer, propulsive ride. Different versions of NITRO™ foam are tuned for different purposes, whether that's delivering maximum speed on race day or balanced cushioning for daily miles. The New Balance 1080 v15 is the best overall daily running shoe for comfort and smooth everyday miles. Top Running Shoes by Category Best Daily Trainer: New Balance 1080 v15 ($160–$170) offers soft, plush foam and a light feel for daily runs. Best for Beginners: ASICS Novablast 6 ($140–$155) gives you high energy return and good protection without a heavy build. Best Max Cushion: HOKA Bondi 9 ($140–$175) features a thick bed of soft foam that absorbs impact on long recovery days. Best Stability: Brooks Adrenaline GTS 25 ($155) uses GuideRails technology to keep your stride steady and secure. Best Lightweight / Speed: adidas Adizero EVO SL ($130–$150) delivers a fast, bouncy ride for tempo workouts at a lower price than carbon-plated shoes.
